question: Which new nuclear-power rules are final, and which are still only proposed?
answer: Of the 8 nuclear rulemakings filed since February 2026 in the record, 2 are final: NRC Part 53, the advanced-reactor licensing framework (published March 30, 2026, effective April 29, 2026) and the NRC's fiscal-2026 fee rule (published June 16, 2026, effective August 17, 2026). 5 are still proposals only: Worker Safety and Health Requirements To Support Reform of Nuclear Reactor Testing; Regulatory Framework for Fusion Machines; Streamlining Contested Adjudications in Licensing Proceedings; NRC Reviews of Reactor Designs Previously Authorized by DOE or Department of War; Licensing Requirements for Microreactors and Other Reactors With Comparable Risk Profiles. The exceptions from foreign ownership, control or domination rule is filed as a proposal, but the factual spine records that a companion direct final rule was confirmed and took effect July 7, 2026. Nothing in these homes shows any of the proposals finalized since.

items.label: Proposed, with a companion direct final rule in effect

sections.title: Rule by rule
sections.sub: Kind, dates and summary are the record's; clocks and meaning are the factual spine's September 2026 reconciliation.

items.title: Worker Safety and Health Requirements To Support Reform of Nuclear Reactor Testing
items.text: DOE proposed amending its 10 CFR Part 851 worker safety regulations to expedite review, approval, and deployment of advanced reactors — including the qualified test reactors in the Reactor Pilot Program — consistent with EO 14301. The comment period was reopened after an AFL-CIO extension request, signaling labor friction over the deregulatory pace.
kv: 10 CFR 851, worker safety, EO 14301, test reactors, labor
Original NOPR published 2026-01-21; extension request dated 2026-02-04; reopening signed 2026-02-24; filed 2026-02-25 08:45; published 2026-02-26, 91 FR 9498–9499; comments through 2026-03-23.

Reopened comments on the January 21 proposed Part 851 rule through March 23. The AFL-CIO request cited review time and affiliate coordination; it is not itself evidence of substantive opposition or a final rule.

sources.label: Federal Register: Worker Safety and Health Requirements To Support Reform of Nuclear Reactor Testing

items.title: Regulatory Framework for Fusion Machines
items.text: The NRC proposed regulating commercial fusion machines under its existing byproduct-material framework — a lighter touch than fission licensing — with technology-inclusive requirements spanning the variety of anticipated fusion designs. The ADVANCE Act's relabeling of 'fusion reactor' to 'fusion machine' anchors the lighter posture meant to clear a path for commercial fusion.
kv: fusion, byproduct material, ADVANCE Act, technology-inclusive, commercialization

Dated 2026-02-23; filed 2026-02-25 at 08:45 (timezone not specified in filing line); published 2026-02-26, 91 FR 9476–9498. Comments due 2026-05-27. NRC selected the Part 30 approach on 2023-04-13. NEIMA enacted 2019-01-14 already set 2027-12-31; ADVANCE enacted 2024-07-09 retained that date and separately required a section 205(c) report within one year (2025-07-09). No final-rule effective date established by this proposal.

Proposed Part 30 byproduct-material framework, following NRC’s 2023 policy choice and ADVANCE’s substantive definitions. The pre-existing NEIMA deadline and state/project licensing clocks remain separate.

sources.label: Federal Register: Regulatory Framework for Fusion Machines

items.title: Streamlining Contested Adjudications in Licensing Proceedings
items.text: The NRC proposed revising its rules of practice to compress contested hearings in licensing proceedings, responding to both the ADVANCE Act of 2024 and EO 14300. The change tightens intervention and filing windows to keep reactor licensing on the EO-mandated accelerated timeline.
kv: adjudication, ADVANCE Act, EO 14300, hearings, licensing
Proposed changes to merits submissions, discovery and contested proceedings. Filing windows vary; appeals sit outside the fixed EO timeline.

sources.label: Federal Register: Streamlining Contested Adjudications in Licensing Proceedings

items.title: NRC Reviews of Reactor Designs Previously Authorized by DOE or Department of War
items.text: The NRC proposed letting commercial reactor applicants directly leverage prior DOE or Department of War authorizations of demonstration reactors into NRC licensing reviews, building a bridge from the DOE pilot/test-reactor track to commercial licensing. A concrete mechanism for converting fast-tracked test reactors into licensed commercial plants.
kv: design leveraging, DOE authorization, demonstration reactors, licensing efficiency
Proposed reuse of tested DOE/Defense safety evidence in NRC review, with a mapping to NRC requirements and changed conditions. Authorization alone does not convert into a commercial license.

sources.label: Federal Register: NRC Reviews of Reactor Designs Previously Authorized by DOE or Department of War

items.title: Licensing Requirements for Microreactors and Other Reactors With Comparable Risk Profiles
items.text: The NRC proposed a new 10 CFR Part 57 framework for rapid, high-volume licensing of microreactors, explicitly responding to EO 14300's direction to consider regulating microreactors through general licenses. The rule would create flexible licensing pathways and reduce regulatory burden for mass-deployed small reactors.
kv: microreactors, Part 57, EO 14300, general license, high-volume
Proposed optional microreactor path for qualifying designs, with conditional construction permission and separate operating approval. The May 15 correction does not finalize the framework.

sources.label: Federal Register: Licensing Requirements for Microreactors and Other Reactors With Comparable Risk Profiles

items.title: Exceptions From Foreign Ownership, Control or Domination

badge.text: Proposed; companion direct final rule in effect

items.text: The NRC proposed carving exceptions to the Atomic Energy Act's foreign-ownership bar for reactor licensees, implementing Section 301 of the ADVANCE Act of 2024. The change opens U.S. reactor projects to allied foreign capital and ownership the AEA had previously blocked.
kv: foreign ownership, ADVANCE Act, FOCD, investment

Proposal and direct final dated 2026-04-06; filed 2026-04-22 08:45; published 2026-04-23. Confirmation dated 2026-06-03; filed 2026-06-04 08:45; published 2026-06-05. Direct final effective 2026-07-07.

The companion April 23 direct final rule was confirmed June 5 as effective July 7. Exceptions concern listed eligible foreign interests in utilization facilities, subject to NRC’s non-inimicality determination; production-facility restrictions remain.

The ownership entry has a confirmed later state: the April 23 direct final rule and June 5 confirmation establish July 7 effectiveness. The 37 listed jurisdictions comprise 36 eligible OECD members plus India; the July 9, 2024 statutory sanctions screen excludes Turkey. Eligibility is not evidence of a completed investment or an approved ownership structure. The May 15 Part 57 correction corrects the proposal’s presentation, without establishing adoption.
The record files this as a proposed rule; the factual spine records the companion direct final rule as in effect. Both are kept.

sources.label: Federal Register: Exceptions From Foreign Ownership, Control or Domination

items.title: Risk-Informed, Technology-Inclusive Regulatory Framework for Advanced Reactors (10 CFR Part 53)
items.text: The NRC finalized 10 CFR Part 53, a new optional, technology-inclusive licensing pathway built for non-light-water advanced reactor designs, fulfilling a mandate of the Nuclear Energy Innovation and Modernization Act. It gives developers a third licensing route alongside the legacy Part 50 and Part 52 frameworks.
kv: Part 53, NEIMA, advanced reactors, technology-inclusive, licensing

Rule dated 2026-03-25; filed 2026-03-27 08:45; published 2026-03-30, 91 FR 15696; effective 2026-04-29. Correction dated 2026-04-09; filed 2026-04-10 08:45; published 2026-04-13; effective 2026-04-29.

Optional commercial fission licensing alongside Parts 50 and 52, including light-water designs. Effective April 29; the April 13 correction retained that date. Fusion has a separate rulemaking; this is distinct from the broader EO 14300 overhaul.

sources.label: Federal Register: Risk-Informed, Technology-Inclusive Regulatory Framework for Advanced Reactors (10 CFR Part 53)

items.title: Fee Schedules; Fee Recovery for Fiscal Year 2026
items.text: The NRC finalized fixed caps on service fees to implement Section 5(a) of EO 14300, directly attacking the hourly-billing model the order condemned for throttling reactor development. The caps are framed as delivering cost predictability and accountability to license applicants.
kv: fee caps, EO 14300, NEIMA, cost predictability, NRC reform

Dated 2026-06-05; filed 2026-06-15 08:45; published 2026-06-16, 91 FR 36470–36509. General effectiveness 2026-08-17; fixed caps start 2026-10-01. Hourly rates begin with the first full pay period after general effectiveness.
Final fee rule generally effective August 17; fixed caps begin October 1. Hourly billing remains. Caps cover requested activities involving a final safety evaluation; decision deadlines are deferred.

sources.label: Federal Register: Fee Schedules; Fee Recovery for Fiscal Year 2026

items.title: Executive Order 14299 — Deploying Advanced Nuclear Reactor Technologies for National Security
items.text: Signed May 23, 2025, orders deployment of advanced reactors — Gen III+, SMRs, microreactors, and mobile reactors — to power critical defense installations and AI data centers, framing energy disruption as a strategic risk. It tasks the Departments of Defense and Energy with siting reactors on federal and military land.
kv: EO 14299, national security, microreactors, SMR, defense
Separate Defense and DOE assignments connect national-security missions, sites and fuel. The Defense operating target is September 30, 2028; the DOE first-site goal is thirty months after signing.

items.title: Executive Order 14300 — Ordering the Reform of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission
items.text: Signed May 23, 2025, this order directs a wholesale overhaul of the NRC, faulting it for licensing only a fraction of reactors since 1978 and for fee structures that throttle development. It mandates fixed fee caps, an 18-month deadline for new reactor license decisions, and a culture shift away from radiation-risk conservatism toward enabling deployment.
kv: NRC reform, EO 14300, licensing, 18-month deadline, nuclear
NRC reform direction: decision deadlines and hourly-fee recovery caps require implementation. The approximately 100-to-400 GW aspiration for 2050 is in section 2(c).

items.title: Executive Order 14301 — Reforming Nuclear Reactor Testing at the Department of Energy
items.text: Signed May 23, 2025, directs DOE to use its own Atomic Energy Act authorization process to fast-track construction and testing of advanced reactors — microreactors, SMRs, Gen III+/IV designs — at DOE sites outside the national labs. The legal foundation for the DOE Reactor Pilot Program, bypassing the slower NRC commercial-licensing path for test reactors.
kv: EO 14301, DOE, reactor testing, advanced reactors, pilot program

DOE laboratory testing and the separate outside-laboratory pilot have different processes. The latter requires sufficient DOE control, not DOE ownership of the land; its research jurisdiction excludes commercial electric-power production.

items.title: Executive Order 14302 — Reinvigorating the Nuclear Industrial Base
items.text: Signed May 23, 2025, targets the full nuclear fuel supply chain — uranium mining, milling, conversion, enrichment, and spent-fuel recycling — and authorizes Defense Production Act voluntary agreements among domestic nuclear companies. It aims to quadruple U.S. nuclear capacity by 2050 and rebuild fuel-cycle independence.
kv: EO 14302, fuel cycle, enrichment, Defense Production Act, reprocessing

Fuel-cycle, workforce, financing and voluntary-agreement directions. Section 4(a) targets five GW of uprates and ten large reactors with complete designs under construction by 2030; the 2050 capacity aspiration belongs to EO 14300.

uncertain: Reading scope: the short prior-design proposal, ownership instruments and confirmation were read substantively; the long Part 57, adjudication, fusion and fee rules received selected scope, authority, clock and operative-clause checks. This is a review of the six original filings and their identified correction/confirmation chain, not a full technical review or a later-finality census of every proposal.
The record labels the foreign-ownership filing a proposed rule; the factual spine records its companion direct final rule as in effect. Both readings are shown on its card.
Effective dates and comment deadlines come from the factual spine, not the record's rows.
A final rule is a legal path, not a licensed or operating reactor.

catalog_context.title: How Washington plans to turn science strategy into funded work
catalog_context.answer: Seventeen countries endorsed the White House science blueprint in Kyoto. The October 8 U.S. summit named new Genesis project selections, compute credits and research tools, but each still needs its own award, access and operating proof.
